Emma Tucker
 
The Heirs to Jack Daniel’s Are Fighting to Keep Control
 
Plus, Russia’s military tests its readiness for a fresh mobilization push, and we take you inside Wall Street’s exclusive wilderness retreat
 
 
IMAGN IMAGES VIA REUTERS CONNECT
 

1. FROM MY DESK

 

The heirs to one of America’s biggest liquor fortunes are in the middle of an intense family drama. Profits at Brown-Forman are shrinking, and shares in the spirits company have lost 60% of their value over five years. People are drinking less of its flagship Jack Daniel’s whiskey, the CEO is leaving, and a crosstown rival has made a $15 billion hostile takeover bid. Laura Cooper takes us inside the rift among some family members who have controlled the company for more than 150 years.

 

And bourbon country isn’t the only place where things are getting heated. Tensions are rising in retirement communities thanks to baby boomers smoking more pot. Seniors are among the fastest-growing demographics for marijuana use, and their neighbors are fuming.

 

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here. If you’re reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

 
 
 

2. TODAY’S HEADLINES

 

• The U.S. and Canada are spiraling toward an all-out trade war. Here’s what to know about the escalating fight.

 

• Democrats still have a path to winning back the Senate, with strength in Georgia and North Carolina and increasingly competitive races in redder states, though Michigan and Maine remain question marks.

 

• Russia is carrying out readiness exercises for a potential new military mobilization, as recent recruit numbers have failed to make up for casualties on the battlefield.

 

• British high-school graduates are increasingly skipping college for white-collar apprenticeships as they question the value of a degree in a job market reshaped by AI.

 
 
 

3. FROM THE MARKETS

 

• Paramount is preparing to begin settlement talks with California officials over the lawsuit standing in the way of its $81 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery.

 

• President Trump’s investment accounts made more than 1,000 stock trades in June, including million-dollar purchases of Berkshire Hathaway, Visa and Mastercard. The White House says independent managers handle the trades.

 
 
 

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

 

We went to Wall Street’s exclusive wilderness camp. Everyone was spooked by AI.

 

About 25 years ago, veteran money manager David Kotok started bringing a group of market wonks to a tiny town in Maine. The gathering has since become an invite-only fishing retreat for financiers, policymakers and subject-matter experts. Our reporter Hannah Erin Lang went to Camp Kotok for a firsthand look. What she heard in candid conversations between canoe outings and poker games made one thing clear: Wall Street’s anxiety about AI is reaching new heights. The paradox of the AI trade was fully on display as investors continue to question the hype but keep pouring money into it.

 

5.

 

Nvidia is making a $6 billion bet on an American alternative to Chinese AI.

 

The American AI industry has poured far more resources into proprietary, or “closed,” models, while Chinese companies have rapidly advanced open-weight models that can be cheaper to operate and easily customized. Now Nvidia is planning to use a $6 billion deal with startup Poolside to build one of the world’s most powerful open-weight AI models, reports Robbie Whelan. The chip giant is betting its Nemotron project can produce a version that rivals the best frontier models within the next year.

 
 
 

Make the most of your next trip.

MESSAGE FROM: MARKETWATCH

6. SEE THE STORY

 

Chasing solar eclipses around the world is strangely addictive.

 
 
ALBERT BONSFILLS FOR WSJ
 

Birds hush. Dogs bark. People grin and gasp, some with tears streaming down their faces. Pamela Paul got hooked on total solar eclipses in 2017 and has been chasing them ever since. Her latest trip took her to the cliffs outside León, Spain, where eclipse chasers from all over the world gathered to witness the otherworldly event.

 
 
 

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEK

 

• Tuesday: South Carolina GOP primary runoff.

 

• Wednesday: Nvidia earnings after markets close; the Commerce Department releases the July PCE index, the Federal Reserve’s preferred inflation gauge.

 

• Thursday: The Fed’s Jackson Hole Symposium kicks off.

 

• Friday: Ridley Scott’s post-apocalyptic film “The Dog Stars” lands in movie theaters. Check out our arts & culture calendar for more.

 
 
 

8. THE NUMBER

 
177%
 

That’s how much Moderna shares surged on Wednesday, after the company and its partner Merck reported successful late-stage trial results for their personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine. The rally helped lift Moderna’s market value from about $25 billion before the announcement to roughly $60 billion by week’s end. Yet the financial math is sobering, David Wainer writes.

 
 
 

9. AND FINALLY…

 

Could you beat a high-schooler on a personal-finance test?

 

More than half of U.S. states now require students to complete a stand-alone personal-finance course to graduate. This coming school year, the College Board is rolling out a new AP Business with Personal Finance course designed in part to boost students’ personal-finance competency. Try a few questions from the test to see how you would fare.

 
 
 

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

 

• WSJ | Buy Side: Auto-loan rates aren’t likely to head lower anytime soon. If you have good credit, you might qualify for a better-than-average loan-refinance rate.
